resources.string: Dots along the edges of the screen follow the motion on the go. Your eyes and body agree again, and motion sickness fades.
This device lacks the required motion sensors

The dots are drawn over other apps, which requires a permission.\n\nIn the list that opens, find “Giro” and turn on “Allow display over other apps”. Then come back here and the effect will turn on by itself.
Dots and motion as close as possible to Vehicle Motion Cues in iOS: white on the dark theme, black on the light one. Other dot and motion settings are unavailable.
Like in iOS: the dots respond to speeding up, braking and turns on the go, then smoothly return. Turning the phone in your hand doesn’t interfere.
Like most Android apps: the dots are anchored to the world around you and respond to any turn or tilt of the phone.
How strongly the dots respond to motion, in either mode
Over the shade and system windows
Dots appear over apps, but under the notification shade and the keyboard
Dots appear over everything, white and black only, without transparency
Turn on the “Giro” service in Accessibility settings
Over the shade and system windows

Only accessibility services, such as the screen magnifier, can draw over the notification shade, the keyboard and system windows.
Open Accessibility settings, choose “Giro” and turn the service on. It reads nothing from the screen and only shows the dots.
If the app was not installed from Google Play, Android may first ask you to allow restricted settings: Settings → Apps → Giro → ⋮ → “Allow restricted settings”.
Giro shows motion cue dots over the notification shade, the keyboard and system windows. The service does not read screen content and does not collect data.
